newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria oil industry to face hard times.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria oil industry to face hard times.

text.p: Nigeria's oil industry and the six multinationals operating in the country could face hard times this year because of a 40 percent cut in joint venture budgets by the military government, the head of a multinational said.

"The funding of the upstream section of the oil industry has certainly not improved. With the 1997 budget, it has substantially deteriorated," Yngvar Heide, managing director of Elf Petroleum Nigeria Limited said in Lagos this week in comments reported by the state news agency on Thursday.
Heide said the industry operated without an approved budget last year and with this year's slash, the sector had lost to other priorities.
In the fiscal budget announced in January, government voted $2.05 billion, the same as last year, for cash calls on projects state-run oil company NNPC operates jointly with the multinationals.
Cash calls are NNPC's payments for any joint projects.

The 40 percent cut refers to the $3.32 billion budget which the joint ventures presented collectively to the governement for 1997. The government opted instead to freeze the budget at last year's level.
The multinationals are Royal Dutch Shell, Mobil Nigeria and Texaco. Others are Chevron Nigeria, Elf Nigeria and Agip.
Heide said: "We thought the situation will improve this year. The option of raising funds from elsewhere in anticipation of reimbursement later is difficult.

"And if Elf for instance must stay afloat, it must take a painful decision of suspending some projects...This will not only affect our growth but will also threaten the oil industry because of its spread." Nigeria produces nearly two million barrels of crude oil per day from which it earns slightly more than 90 percent of its foreign earnings.
